QUIC Retry packet creation and verification with token and integrity tag handling.

# Purpose
This C file implements QUIC `Retry` packet handling. It contains code to build the Retry pseudo-packet used for integrity protection, create a server Retry packet, and verify Retry packets on both the server side and the client side. The main data handled here are QUIC connection IDs, Retry tokens, packet headers, and the Retry integrity tag. The file also uses AES-GCM helpers to sign and verify the token and the packet integrity data.

The public functions in the file are [`fd_quic_retry_pseudo`](<#fd_quic_retry_pseudo>), [`fd_quic_retry_create`](<#fd_quic_retry_create>), [`fd_quic_retry_server_verify`](<#fd_quic_retry_server_verify>), and [`fd_quic_retry_client_verify`](<#fd_quic_retry_client_verify>). [`fd_quic_retry_create`](<#fd_quic_retry_create>) builds a Retry packet from an incoming Initial packet, stores the original destination connection ID and source connection ID, and adds the token and integrity tag. [`fd_quic_retry_server_verify`](<#fd_quic_retry_server_verify>) checks that a received Retry token matches the source address, port, and time limits that were stored when the token was created. [`fd_quic_retry_client_verify`](<#fd_quic_retry_client_verify>) parses a Retry packet, extracts the Retry token and source connection ID, and verifies the Retry integrity tag before the client accepts the packet.
